airport.name: Grosseto Corrado Baccarini Air Base / Grosseto Airport

summary: Grosseto Corrado Baccarini Air Base (GRS/LIRS) is a joint-use military and civilian airport located approximately 3 km west of the city of Grosseto in the Maremma region of southern Tuscany, Italy. Originally developed as a military airfield during the early 20th century, it is named after Corrado Baccarini, an Italian military aviation pioneer. The facility primarily serves Italian Air Force operations but also accommodates limited general aviation and charter flights, offering visitors a gateway to Tuscany's coastal and archaeological attractions.
faqs:
Q: Does Grosseto Airport handle commercial passenger flights?
A: The airport has limited scheduled commercial service and is mainly oriented toward general aviation, private flights, and military operations. Travelers should check with operators for any seasonal or charter availability.

Q: Is the airport shared between military and civilian use?
A: Yes, it is a joint-use facility. Italian Air Force activities take precedence, but civilian traffic, including private and general aviation, is also accommodated.

Q: What region of Italy is the airport in?
A: It is located in the Maremma area of southern Tuscany, near the Tyrrhenian coast, about 150 km south of Florence.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities available?
A: As a controlled military-civilian airfield, handling international general aviation flights is possible, but travelers should coordinate customs arrangements in advance through their handler or operator.
transport_tips: The airport is just a short 5-10 minute drive from Grosseto city center, making taxi or pre-arranged car service the most convenient option. Public transport connections are limited, so renting a car at the airport or in town is recommended for exploring the wider Maremma region. The SS1 Aurelia highway nearby provides easy road access to the Tuscan coast and inland destinations.
local_tip: If you're flying in privately, request permission and PPR (prior permission required) well in advance through the military operations office, and time your arrival outside restricted military training windows—early mornings and weekdays tend to be smoother for civilian operations.
